costGuide.title: Jeep ENS 2.8 CRD Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an ENS 2.8 CRD typically takes 10-14 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent) - the inline-four layout is simpler than a V6, but engine bay packaging in the Grand Cherokee WK adds complexity. Confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: (All figures . Fitted = supply price + labour band below.)

What genuinely moves the price for this engine is whether the injectors have been serviced or replaced - these are a common failure point and cost £300-£800 each for genuine units. The EGR cooler condition is also critical; a failed cooler can lead to coolant loss and overheating. Timing chain and tensioner condition matters significantly - if the chain has stretched or the tensioner has failed, the engine is likely uneconomical to repair without a full overhaul. failures.title: Jeep ENS 2.8 CRD Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: EGR cooler failure - coolant loss
items.whatHappens: The EGR cooler on the 2.8 CRD can develop internal cracks, allowing coolant to leak into the exhaust or be burned off. Symptoms include persistently low coolant levels, poor heater performance, and eventually engine overheating. This is one of the most common complaints on the 2.8 CRD .
items.repairVsReplace: EGR cooler replacement (£400-£800) is the fix. If ignored and the engine overheats, head gasket failure can occur, significantly increasing repair costs.

items.title: Injector failure - rough running and poor starting
items.whatHappens: The 2.8 CRD uses common-rail injectors that can fail or suffer from "leak-off" issues. Symptoms include rough idle, poor cold starting, reduced power, excessive smoke, and increased fuel consumption .
items.repairVsReplace: Injector replacement is the fix - genuine Bosch units cost £300-£800 each depending on the supplier. All four should ideally be replaced at the same time. If ignored, unburnt fuel can contaminate the oil and cause bottom-end damage.

items.title: Timing chain and tensioner wear - rattle on startup
items.whatHappens: The 2.8 CRD has a timing chain that can stretch over time. The tensioner can also wear, causing rattle on cold start. If the chain stretches or jumps, catastrophic engine damage occurs .
items.repairVsReplace: Timing chain replacement is a significant job (£800-£1,500 at an independent). If the chain has already jumped, cylinder head or piston damage is likely - at which point a full engine replacement becomes the only viable option.

items.title: Turbocharger wear - loss of power and smoking
items.whatHappens: The turbocharger on the 2.8 CRD can suffer from oil seal failure or bearing wear. Symptoms include excessive smoke (blue or black), loss of power, and whistling noises from the turbo .
items.repairVsReplace: Turbocharger rebuild or replacement (£500-£1,200) is the fix. If the turbo has failed catastrophically, metal debris can be ingested into the engine, requiring a full rebuild or replacement.

failures.goodYearsLine: The 2.8 CRD was updated during its production run. Later examples (2009-2012) benefit from revised injectors and ECU calibration, though the EGR cooler and timing chain issues remain across all years. Regular oil changes (every 5,000 miles) using the correct 5W-40 fully synthetic oil is essential for longevity.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the ENS 2.8 CRD
variants.intro: The ENS is one of several codes in the VM Motori RA 428 / 2.8 CRD family. Understanding the differences matters when buying a replacement - not all 2.8-litre diesels are interchangeable. Where to find the engine code: - On the engine block - a stamped label on the front or side of the engine - On the V5C registration document under "Engine number" - the ENS code appears in the first three characters - On the driver's door pillar or under-bonnet VIN/engine sticker - Via a VIN decoder - enter your full 17-digit VIN online to confirm the factory engine code Common confusions: | Similar code | Difference | Link | |--------------|------------|------| | ENR | 2.8L CRD variant with different ECU calibration (lower output, Euro 4 emissions) | [ENR engine] | | ENC / ENJ / ENS (earlier) | Earlier VM Motori 2.8 CRD family - different injection system and ECU | [ENC/ENJ engines] | | ENC / ENJ / ENS (later) | Later 2.8 CRD (2009-2012) with DPF and revised emissions hardware | [ENC/ENJ engines] | | EXF | 3.0 EcoDiesel V6 - completely different engine | [EXF engine] (see previous page) |

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement ENS 2.8 CRD - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used ENS can make sense for older Grand Cherokee or Cherokee examples where vehicle value doesn't justify a recon unit. However - insist on documented service history and evidence that injectors and EGR cooler have been addressed. Timing chain rattle on cold start is a red flag; walk away from any unit that doesn't start cold and run smoothly. Given the age of these engines (2005-2012), many used units are high-mileage and near the end of their service life.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper ENS recon addresses the known weak points - EGR cooler replacement, injector overhaul or replacement, timing chain and tensioner renewal, and full gasket and seal replacement. The turbocharger is also inspected and rebuilt where necessary. With 12-24 months warranty, this is the safest route for most owners, particularly as these engines approach 15-20 years old.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild of the ENS is usually only justified for low-mileage, high-value examples (e.g., a cherished Grand Cherokee WK Overland with under 60,000 miles). The rebuild must include new timing chain and tensioner, new injectors, new EGR cooler, new turbocharger (or full rebuild), and new pistons and rings. This is the "zero-risk" option - but at £3,500-£5,500 supply-only, it's only viable for vehicles worth over £8,000.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Fitting through our network of vetted UK Jeep and diesel specialists - supply-only or full supply and fit, with nationwide delivery and warranty cover on every reconditioned and rebuilt unit.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The ENS sits in vehicles with modest value ranges in 2025 - a 2005 Grand Cherokee WK may be worth £2,000-£4,000, while a 2012 Cherokee KK might be worth £3,000-£6,000. Given these values, evaluate carefully before committing to a replacement. A used engine with documented injector and EGR cooler history may be the only financially sensible option for lower-value examples. If the vehicle is worth less than £3,000, consider whether a replacement is justified at all - a £2,200 reconditioned engine plus £800 labour could easily exceed the vehicle's value. Always factor in the full fitted cost before proceeding.

items.question: What is the most common failure on the Jeep ENS 2.8 CRD engine?
items.answer: The most common failures are EGR cooler cracking (causing coolant loss), injector failure (rough running, poor starting), and timing chain tensioner wear (rattle on cold start). EGR cooler failure typical onset is 60,000-100,000 miles; leads to overheating if ignored. Injector failure typical onset is 80,000-120,000 miles; symptoms include rough idle, excessive smoke. Timing chain wear typical onset is 80,000-120,000 miles; ignoring can cause catastrophic engine damage.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned ENS 2.8 CRD engine?
items.answer: A used ENS is viable only if it has full documented service history and evidence that the injectors, EGR cooler, and timing chain have been addressed - otherwise, you're buying a high-mileage time bomb. Given the age of these engines (15-20 years), many used units are near the end of their service life. A reconditioned unit is the better choice for most owners, as it addresses the known weak points and includes a 12-24 month warranty. However, always factor in the vehicle's value - a £2,200 recon plus labour may exceed the value of a £3,000 Grand Cherokee. Browse reconditioned ENS engines with warranty.

items.question: What is the difference between ENS, ENR, and ENJ codes?
items.answer: They are all 2.8 CRD family engines but have different specifications. ENS is the standard 2.8 CRD fitted to most UK Jeep models (150-177 hp). ENR is a lower-output variant (approx. 140 hp) with different ECU calibration and Euro 4 emissions. ENC/ENJ are earlier injection systems and ECU hardware - not a direct swap with ENS without significant work. Always confirm your exact code before ordering - fitting the wrong variant may require reprogramming or different ancillaries.

items.question: How do I confirm my Jeep has the ENS engine code?
items.answer: Check three places: the engine block itself (a stamped label on the front or side of the inline-four), your V5C registration document under "Engine number" (the first three characters should be "ENS"), and use a VIN decoder online with your full 17-digit VIN to pull the factory build sheet. Given the confusion with other 2.8 CRD codes, always verify the physical label before ordering.
